-- proof of pattern exhaustivity. Reachable pattern arms are unchanged.
Function.const _ default)

/-- Convert a Sail integer to a Lean natural only when its value is nonnegative.
    A violated Sail range is reported, never silently clamped to zero. -/
def Int.toNatChecked (n : _root_.Int) : Nat :=
  if 0 ≤ n then n.toNat else panic! "Sail.Int.toNatChecked: negative integer"

@[simp] theorem Int.toNatChecked_of_nonneg (n : _root_.Int) (h : 0 ≤ n) :
    Int.toNatChecked n = n.toNat := by
  simp [Int.toNatChecked, h]

/-- L5 / C13: explicit width cast emitted by the generator where Sail's typechecker proved two
widths equal from constraints Lean does not see (e.g. `hi - lo + 1` with variable indices vs `n`).
Identity cast when the widths agree; otherwise it panics (a generator/runtime bug, never a silent
resize -- run executables with `LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC=1` to make it fatal). -/
@[inline] def castWidth {n m : Nat} (x : BitVec n) : BitVec m :=
  if h : n = m then h ▸ x else panic! "Sail.BitVec.castWidth: width mismatch"

@[simp] theorem castWidth_eq {n : Nat} (x : BitVec n) : castWidth (m := n) x = x := by
  simp [castWidth]

/-- Sail `set_slice_int len n lo x`: replace bits `[lo, lo+len)` of the unbounded
two's-complement integer `n` with `x` (sail.c: `mpz_set` then `mpz_setbit`/`mpz_clrbit`
for each slice bit). All other bits of `n`, including its sign extension, are kept.
`(n / 2^lo) % 2^len` is the current field (Int `/` and `%` are Euclidean, i.e. floor for
the positive divisor, which is the two's-complement view for negative `n`). -/
n - ((n / 2 ^ lo) % 2 ^ len) * 2 ^ lo + (x.toNat : Int) * 2 ^ lo

  | FuelExhausted (site : String)
  /-- Fork (integration): a real operation with no exact result (Isla `RealInexact`): `sqrt_real` of a
  value whose square root the `SailReal` instance cannot represent exactly. Never an approximation. -/

/-- Static label of a nondeterministic choice (an `undefined_*` / `internal_pick` call site).
The Sail-to-Lean backend emits one label per call site, so a labelled draw reads the oracle
without advancing any state: two control-flow paths that perform different draws still end in
the same state, which lets a specializer merge them.
* `site n`    : call site `n`, statically checked to execute at most once per top-level call.
* `occ n k`   : `k`-th dynamic execution of call site `n` (sites that may execute repeatedly:
                inside loops, recursive functions, or helpers invoked more than once).
* `child ℓ i` : `i`-th draw inside a generated `undefined_<T>` initialiser called with label `ℓ`.
* `anon k`    : `k`-th unlabelled draw (legacy `choose`; hand-written code only). -/
inductive ChoiceLabel where
  | site (n : Nat)
  | occ (n k : Nat)
  | child (parent : ChoiceLabel) (i : Nat)
  | anon (k : Nat)
  deriving DecidableEq, Hashable, Repr, Inhabited

/-- Labelled draw: the value chosen at label `ℓ`; does not change the choice state. -/
  (chooseAt : ∀ p : Sail.Primitive, ChoiceLabel → α → p.reflect)

/-- An arbitrary oracle: one value for every (label, primitive type). -/
abbrev Oracle := ChoiceLabel → (p : Sail.Primitive) → p.reflect

/-- The universal choice source. Its state is an arbitrary oracle (plus the counter of legacy
unlabelled draws), so a statement quantified over the machine state is quantified over every
resolution of every nondeterministic choice. Generated models use this source; nothing fixes a
choice to a constant. -/
def oracleChoiceSource : ChoiceSource where
  α := Oracle × Nat
  nextState _ s := (s.1, s.2 + 1)
  choose p s := s.1 (.anon s.2) p
  chooseAt p ℓ s := s.1 ℓ p

/-- Fork (H3, effects as events): an architectural side effect of the sequential model, appended to
`SequentialState.events` in program order. Payloads are the model's own `Arch` types, so for Arm a
barrier event carries the full `Barrier` value (`Barrier_DMB`/`Barrier_DSB` with domain, types and
nXS, `Barrier_ISB`, `Barrier_SSBB`, `Barrier_PSSBB`, `Barrier_SB`, and any constructor a splice adds,
e.g. CSDB). Memory events record the physical address, the size in bytes, the virtual address (if
any), the access kind and the tag request; a write also records the value written. A memory event is
logged when the request is issued, before the access, so a faulting access still leaves its event. -/
inductive Event [Arch] where
  | barrier (b : Arch.barrier)
  /-- Fork (integration): a barrier with no constructor in the model's (non-scattered) barrier union,
  added by a splice through its own extension union (Arm: `BarrierExt.Barrier_CSDB`); carries the
  constructor's `repr`, so it stays distinct from every `Arch.barrier` value. -/
  | barrierExt (desc : String)

| tlbi (op : Arch.tlb_op)
  | translationStart (ts : Arch.trans_start)
  | translationEnd (te : Arch.trans_end)
  | takeException (f : Arch.fault)
  | returnException (pa : Arch.pa)
  | memRead (pa : Nat) (size : Nat) (va : Option Nat) (kind : Access_kind Arch.arch_ak) (tag : Bool)
  | memWrite (pa : Nat) (size : Nat) (va : Option Nat) (kind : Access_kind Arch.arch_ak)
      (value : Option (BitVec (8 * size))) (tag : Option Bool)

/-! Unit tests for `Sail.set_slice_int` / `Sail.get_slice_int` against Sail's reference
semantics (lib/sail.c `set_slice_int`: `mpz_set` then per-bit `mpz_setbit`/`mpz_clrbit`,
GMP's infinite two's-complement view for negative integers). Regression for L4
(the old definition truncated `n` to `len` bits first: `set_slice_int 1 8388608 0 1#1 = -1`). -/

namespace SailTests.SetSliceInt
SailTest/VectorConversion.lean

set_option maxRecDepth 100000

/-- Bit `k` of `n` in the infinite two's-complement view (GMP `mpz_tstbit`). -/
def refTstBit (n : Int) (k : Nat) : Bool := (n / 2 ^ k) % 2 == 1

/-- GMP `mpz_setbit` / `mpz_clrbit`. -/
def refPutBit (n : Int) (k : Nat) (b : Bool) : Int :=
  if refTstBit n k == b then n else if b then n + 2 ^ k else n - 2 ^ k

/-- Literal transcription of sail.c `set_slice_int`. -/
def refSetSliceInt (len : Nat) (n : Int) (lo : Nat) (x : BitVec len) : Int :=
  (List.range len).foldl (fun r i => refPutBit r (lo + i) (x.getLsbD i)) n

-- The L4 regression (FPRoundBase odd rounding: `int_mant[0] = '1'` on 2^23).
example : set_slice_int 1 8388608 0 1#1 = 8388609 := by rfl
example : set_slice_int 1 8388609 0 0#1 = 8388608 := by rfl
-- Field in the middle, wider than the old truncation width.
example : set_slice_int 4 0x12345 4 0xA#4 = 0x123A5 := by rfl
-- Negative integers: two's-complement view, sign extension preserved.
example : set_slice_int 1 (-1) 0 0#1 = -2 := by rfl
example : set_slice_int 8 (-1) 8 0#8 = -65281 := by rfl
example : set_slice_int 4 (-16) 0 0xF#4 = -1 := by rfl
example : set_slice_int 3 (-5) 2 0#3 = -29 := by rfl
-- Zero-length slice is the identity.
example : set_slice_int 0 (-12345) 7 0#0 = -12345 := by rfl

-- Exhaustive small-range agreement with the sail.c transcription.
#guard Id.run do
  let mut ok := true
  for len in List.range 5 do
    for lo in List.range 6 do
      for k in List.range 141 do
        let n : Int := (k : Int) - 70
        for v in List.range (2 ^ len) do
          let x := BitVec.ofNat len v
          if set_slice_int len n lo x != refSetSliceInt len n lo x then ok := false
          -- round trip through get_slice_int
          if get_slice_int len (set_slice_int len n lo x) lo != x then ok := false
  return ok

-- Large magnitudes (beyond 64 bits), both signs.
#guard [((2 : Int) ^ 100 + 12345), -((2 : Int) ^ 100) - 77, (2 : Int) ^ 70 - 1, -1].all fun n =>
  [(0, 0xFF#8), (60, 0x5A#8), (95, 0x81#8)].all fun (lo, x) =>
    set_slice_int 8 n lo x == refSetSliceInt 8 n lo x

end SailTests.SetSliceInt

# Axiom policy

Allowed axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.
No exceptions. New exceptions require explicit release-owner approval, an exact name,
approval date, reason and removal plan. Do not use native evaluation to prove
theorems. `archive/` is historical, excluded from Lake roots, and never imported.
